sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the research page
sections.what: Brings in the React state hook, the settings and run panels from the Controls file, and shared helpers and data types.
sections.why: Likely reason: this page reuses the run history and settings panels rather than repeating them.
sections.watch_out: Changes to those panels also change this page.

sections.name: QUEUE_LABEL
sections.title: Plain descriptions of each queue
sections.what: Gives each of the three queues a plain title and a plain explanation: client research, industry research, and location and capex research.
sections.why: Likely reason: staff see what each queue does without knowing internal names.
sections.watch_out: Every queue kind must have an entry here, or the explainer will fail when that queue appears.

sections.name: QueueExplainer
sections.title: Queue explainer
sections.what: For each queue, shows the number queued, the running count out of the allowed slots, the average time per job, the estimated time to clear, and the last 24 hours' finished and failed counts. Also explains why jobs wait in bursts and why they run a few at a time.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains why research can look slow or bursty, so users do not assume it is broken.
sections.watch_out: If the first queue has no concurrency value, the explanation falls back to three, which may not match the real setting.

sections.name: Research
sections.title: Research page with tabs
sections.what: Shows a bar for each run status, workspace-wide location totals, and four tabs: run history, source log, research notes and settings. Results are limited to the selected account when one is chosen. A note says no evidence means a research gap, not proof that no opportunity exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps everything about research on one page, and the note prevents users reading silence as a clean result.
sections.watch_out: Some source-log text is cut off in the packet, so its details are unverified. Notes only show records that have text or an error.

summary: Shows the research page for opportunity signals: queue status, run status counts, and tabs for run history, source log, research notes and settings.
purpose: Lets staff see whether background research is working, what it has found, and what it could not check.
why: Likely reason: research can look slow or patchy, so the page explains queue timing and marks missing evidence as a gap, not a finding.
how: Filters signals, sources and runs to the selected account when one is chosen. Counts runs by status, shows queue summaries and location totals, and displays the chosen tab.
inputs: The full opportunity state, an optional account id, a function that looks up display names, admin status, refresh and save actions, and a callback when a source is opened.
outputs: A status page with bars, queue cards, a location summary, four tabs, and the run and settings panels from the Controls file.
risks: The explanation text falls back to three parallel jobs when no queue value is available, so the wording may not match the real setting. The status bars divide by the run count, so an empty list shows zero-width bars rather than a warning.
debug: If a queue card is missing, check that its kind has an entry in the label list. If source or note tabs are empty, check the selected account and the stored source and note records. If bars look wrong, check the run statuses.
